title: Seabright Retail — private deploy fieldbook
content:
Meeting context:
- Customer: Seabright Retail (regional grocery chain, ~230 stores across NE US).
- Date: 2024-10-08 quick sync with Seabright infra + security + product.
- Attendees: Ravi (Redwood), Maya (Redwood), Ellen (solutions), Tomás (Seabright infra), Priya (Seabright security), Aaron (Seabright product).

One-liner ask:
- Run a private inference deployment (VPC + on-prem gateway) to support an assistant for store associates: inventory lookup, low-latency restocking suggestions, and in-store customer Q&A. Must remain PCI-light and keep PII off cloud.

High-level constraints (customer stated):
- Primary inference in a regional colo (Equinix) with per-store fat-edge proxies for intermittent connectivity.
- Target 95th percentile latency: <110ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) during normal hours.
- Peak concurrency: 60 concurrent sessions across all stores; steady-state token rate ~120k tokens/min.
- Data residency: model compute in US-east region; logs and telemetry must not contain customer PII; audit retention 2 years.
- Security: HSM-backed key management; require FIPS-validated KMS integration for secrets in the gateway.
- Compliance: customer will remain in PCI scope for card-present interactions — Redwood must ensure transcripts with any card data are redacted client-side.

Notes / gotchas from infra/security:
- Edge proxies use NAT pools; some stores sit behind CGNAT/4G fallback. This impacts our source-IP-based routing and zero-trust mutual TLS.
- Occasional satellite outages (1–2 hrs/month) — must gracefully degrade to local fallback model.
- Colo ops impose strict egress filtering; need explicit IP ranges for health checks and outbound model downloads.
- On-prem gateway runs on RHEL8 VMs; kernel is older (4.18). Expect issues with latest WASM or special kernel drivers for GPU passthrough.
- Storage: they prefer S3-compatible object store in-colo (MinIO). We should avoid relying on cloud-managed S3 endpoints.

Technical options discussed (pros/cons):
1) Private control plane (Redwood-hosted) + customer-managed data plane (recommended initial):
   - Pros: faster onboarding; control plane keeps rollouts/analytics; data plane stays in-customer network.
   - Cons: customer wants assurance logs sent to their logging with PII redaction done before control-plane forwarding.

2) Full air-gapped private deployment (long-term):
   - Pros: minimizes data egress concerns.
   - Cons: longer uplift time, requires signed binaries, extra support retainer; telemetry limited.

3) Dedicated (Redwood-managed) colo nodes (hybrid):
   - Pros: easier to hit latency/SLA; we can guarantee kernel/driver versions.
   - Cons: loses some data residency control; more costly for customer.

Redwood runtime / config suggestions for PoC:
- Model selection: start with 7B float16 variant in dedicated region, quantized 4-bit for edge cache where needed. Keep model pinned to v2024-10-01 for reproducibility.
- Batching: per-device continuous batching with max batch size 16, prefer latency-first policy.
- KV cache TTL: 60s for cross-request prefix reuse; enable prefix caching for store-specific prompts.
- Fallback policy: if colo losing connectivity to control plane, route inference to local distilled model (128M-300M params) for basic retrieval Qs.
- Stream vs non-stream: enable streaming for assistant; enable token-level rate limiter in gateway to protect from runaway prompts.

Operational / observability expectations:
- Token-level cost estimate: provide Seabright with a per-hour estimate for typical shift: ~900k tokens/d per store during promos; use this to size Dedicated vs Private pool.
- Tracing: require distributed tracing header (x-rdwd-trace) to be propagated from edge->data-plane->control-plane. Customer will map to their Splunk traces.
- Alerts: set SLOs for 99th latency (<1s) and error rate (<0.5%); critical alerts routed to Seabright on-call (PagerDuty).

Security integration specifics:
- HSM: Seabright uses Azure Key Vault with HSM; need Redwood to support external KMS plugin. Short term: use envelope encryption with customer-provided keys.
- Redaction: recommend client-side middleware (run in edge proxy) to redact PAN-like patterns and CVV before logs leave store. Provide JS/Go snippet for redaction.
- Audit logging: redact PII before sending to Redwood telemetry; include hashed identifiers only.

Open technical questions (actionable):
- Q1: Can Seabright expose a range of static IPs from colo for model artifact downloads and health checks? (Tomás)
- Q2: Which HSM/KMS APIs (Azure Key Vault SKU) are available in the colo? Need tenant + permission model. (Priya)
- Q3: Edge proxy compute: are GPUs available at edge or will local fallback be CPU-only? (Tomás)
- Q4: Confirm encryption-at-rest policy for MinIO and acceptable ciphers. (Aaron)

Immediate next steps (owner + due dates):
- A1: Draft minimal PoC architecture diagram + network flow (Redwood) — Ravi — due 2024-10-16 — LINK: INF-4871.
- A2: Provide redaction middleware example and integration guide (Redwood dev sample) — Maya — due 2024-10-20 — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/212.
- A3: Seabright to confirm static IP ranges and firewall rules — Tomás — due 2024-10-18.
- A4: Security deep-dive call to map HSM/KMS permissions and acceptable signing flow — Priya + Maya — schedule by 2024-10-22.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Kernel/driver mismatch in colo prevents GPU usage -> Mitigation: plan CPU fallback and consider Redwood-managed colo nodes for early deployment.
- Risk: PII leakage via logs -> Mitigation: mandate client-side redaction and preflight audit before sending any telemetry to control plane.
- Risk: Unexpected token volumes during promotions -> Mitigation: burst autoscaling policy + rate-limited queueing and economical fallback model.

Notes to self (working):
- Keep PoC scoped: core assistant intents (inventory-check, restock-suggest, sku-lookup). Defer advanced personalization until data residency path is finalized.
- Prepare benchmarking script that simulates 150 concurrent short sessions from 230 stores with intermittent 4G latencies. Use this to validate batching config and cache hit assumptions.

Contact/hand-off:
- Seabright primary: Tomás Rivera (infra), Priya Nair (security), Aaron Blake (product).
- Redwood: Ravi Desai (owner), Maya Chen (integration), Ellen Martinez (solutions).

Revision history:
- 2024-10-12 created (initial notes from sync)
- 2024-10-16 updated with action owners and POc model pin
- 2024-11-02 added HSM details and final risk mitigations

End of fieldbook.
